# NYS DREAM Act

## The 2026–27 NYS DREAM Act applications are now open.

The Senator José Peralta New York State DREAM Act gives students who received their high school degree or GED in New York State and students receiving in-state tuition, including undocumented students, access to New York State‐administered student financial aid to support their higher education costs.

results.title: José Peralta New York State Dream Act – The City University of New York
results.content:
The José Peralta New York State DREAM Act allows undocumented and other students access to New York State‐administered grants and scholarships that support their higher education costs. If you attended or graduated from an NYS high school, attended an approved NYS high school equivalency program, or received an NYS equivalency diploma, you may be eligible for state financial aid.

The DREAM Act opens the doors of higher education and provides access to the Excelsior Scholarship, the Tuition Assistance Program (TAP) and other state‐administered scholarships including Opportunity Programs. [...] LEAD Coalition created a eligibility flow chart and video guide. Take a look at it to determine your eligibility:

 NYS Dream Act Module 2 – Eligibility and State Funding
 Eligibility Flow Chart

#### 2. Apply for the York State Dream Act and TAP

To be eligible for TAP as an undocumented student you have to submit TWO applications, 1. the New York State Dream Act and 2. the Tuition Assistance Program application. This second application will be submitted through the New York State Dream Act portal. To see what this looks like take a look at the walk through below.

 NYS Dream Act Preview Walkthrough by Adelante Student Voices [...] If you reached out to either of the two resources above and have not heard back or your campus has not received you TAP award please fill out the following survey and someone from CUNY Immigrant Student Success will reach out to you.

Get help for completed applications

CUNY infographic showing support for immigrant and undocumented students with TAP and Dream Act

#### 4. Consider applying to other State funded Programs

In addition to TAP, the New York State Dream Act also makes you eligible for Opportunity Programs like ASAP, CD, or SEEK. This is a new legislation so some of our campuses may not be up to date on this information. Please visit our guide to help you access state funds provide by ASAP, CD, and SEEK.
